events.tx: The Carriage and Wagon department of the Lancashire and Yorkshire Railway depot at Newton Heath starts a works team. Colours: the railway's green and gold.
The first home ground: a field by the railway yard, its lease paid by the railway company. Home until 1893.
Newton Heath, in green and gold, lose 6–0 to Bolton Wanderers' reserves.
Newton Heath LYR draw 2–2 at Fleetwood Rangers in the first round, the earliest match in the archive.
A regional league that folded before the end of its first season; Newton Heath joined the new Football Alliance in 1889.
1889–1900. 338 matches, 151 won, 56 drawn, 131 lost (45% wins).
First season of league football: 8th of 12 in the new Football Alliance.
Runners-up in the Football Alliance; elected to the enlarged Football League First Division.
A 4–3 defeat at Blackburn Rovers to open the First Division season.
United 10–1 Wolverhampton Wanderers (home), First Division.
Independent of the railway company by the start of 1892–93, the club's first season in the Football League.
The second home, next to a chemical works whose fumes were said to drift over the pitch when Newton Heath were losing. Home until 1910.
16th of 16 in the First Division.
1900–1903. 111 matches, 43 won, 20 drawn, 48 lost (39% wins).
Newton Heath, £2670 in debt, face a winding-up order. Captain Harry Stafford finds four local businessmen, among them brewer John Henry Davies, to invest.
The fresh start gets a new name, with Davies as president; red shirts, white shorts and black socks follow. Club sources give 26 April.
1903–1912. 362 matches, 199 won, 71 drawn, 92 lost (55% wins). 2 First Division titles, 1 FA Cup, 2 Charity Shields.
Promoted: 2nd of 20 in the Second Division.
First Division, Bank Street. Turnbull 3, Meredith. Second game of the season and the one that announced the new side; United won their first ten.
First Division champions: 52 points from 38 games (W23 D6 L9, 81 goals). Manager: Ernest Mangnall.
4–0 in the replay after 1–1 against Queens Park Rangers. Manager: Ernest Mangnall. Scorers: J. Turnbull 3, Wall.

1–0 against Bristol City at Crystal Palace. Manager: Ernest Mangnall. Scorers: S. Turnbull. Both sides wore change strips — United in white with a red V. Turnbull followed up when Halse's shot came back off the bar.
Archibald Leitch's ground, paid for with a £60000 loan from Davies, opens with a 4–3 defeat by Liverpool.
First Division champions: 52 points from 38 games (W22 D8 L8, 72 goals). Manager: Ernest Mangnall. Final day. Word of Villa's defeat at Anfield reached the ground before the end.
8–4 against Swindon Town at Stamford Bridge. Manager: Ernest Mangnall. Scorers: Halse 6, Turnbull, Wall.
1912–1912. 6 matches, 3 won, 2 drawn, 1 lost (50% wins).
1912–1914. 91 matches, 36 won, 19 drawn, 36 lost (40% wins).
1914–1921. 121 matches, 38 won, 36 drawn, 47 lost (31% wins).
1921–1926. 220 matches, 86 won, 58 drawn, 76 lost (39% wins).
22nd of 22 in the First Division.
Promoted: 2nd of 22 in the Second Division.
United 0–7 Blackburn Rovers (away), First Division. The joint heaviest in the club's history.
1926–1927. 31 matches, 9 won, 8 drawn, 14 lost (29% wins).
1927–1931. 200 matches, 61 won, 48 drawn, 91 lost (30% wins).
The club's benefactor since 1902. Without him the finances decline through the next four years.
United 0–7 Aston Villa (away), First Division. The joint heaviest in the club's history.
22nd of 22 in the First Division.
1931–1932. 29 matches, 14 won, 4 drawn, 11 lost (48% wins).
United 0–7 Wolverhampton Wanderers (away), Second Division. The joint heaviest in the club's history.
Close to bankruptcy, United are saved by Gibson's £2000 investment on condition he becomes chairman. He owns the club until his death in 1951.
1932–1937. 235 matches, 92 won, 53 drawn, 90 lost (39% wins). 1 Second Division title.
20th of 22 in the Second Division, the club's lowest league position.
Second Division champions: 56 points from 42 games (W22 D12 L8, 85 goals). Promoted. Manager: Scott Duncan.
21st of 22 in the First Division.
1937–1945. 76 matches, 30 won, 24 drawn, 22 lost (39% wins).
Promoted: 2nd of 22 in the Second Division.
Gibson secures the Cliff as a venue for practice matches and the junior side; it becomes the training ground until 1999.
76962 watch an FA Cup semi-final, Wolverhampton Wanderers v Grimsby Town. Still the ground record.
A German raid three days after football resumed there destroys much of the ground, including the main stand. Offices move to Gibson's Cornbrook Cold Storage; home games move to City's Maine Road.
1945–1969. 1115 matches, 563 won, 261 drawn, 291 lost (50% wins). 5 First Division titles, 2 FA Cups, 5 Charity Shields (inc. 2 shared), 1 European Cup.
FA Cup third round, Villa Park. Rowley 2, Morris 2, Pearson, Delaney. Villa scored inside a minute; United were 5–1 up by half-time.

4–2 against Blackpool at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Matt Busby. Scorers: Rowley 2, Anderson, Pearson. Blackpool, with Matthews and Mortensen, led twice. Rowley's second, a header from Morris's free-kick, turned it.
3–4 against Arsenal at Arsenal Stadium. Manager: Matt Busby.
After eight years at Maine Road, 41748 see the first game at the rebuilt ground: 3–0 against Bolton Wanderers.
Owner and chairman since 1931. His widow, Lillian, keeps the shares; former player Harold Hardman becomes chairman.
First Division champions: 57 points from 42 games (W23 D11 L8, 95 goals). Manager: Matt Busby. Arsenal finished with nine fit men. Carey lifted the trophy a week later in his final home match.
4–2 against Newcastle United at Old Trafford. Manager: Matt Busby. Scorers: Rowley 2, Byrne, Downie.
First Division, Old Trafford. Berry 62 (pen), Taylor 85; Durie 2. 62,277 saw the title clinched. Blackpool led inside two minutes; Taylor's winner came five minutes from time.
First Division champions: 60 points from 42 games (W25 D10 L7, 83 goals). Manager: Matt Busby.
United 10–0 Anderlecht (home), European Cup Preliminary round Second leg.
European Cup preliminary round, Maine Road. Viollet 4, Taylor 3, Whelan 2, Berry. Still the club's record win. Old Trafford had no floodlights yet.
1–0 against Manchester City at Maine Road. Manager: Matt Busby. Scorers: Viollet.
£40000 of floodlights mean European nights no longer go to Maine Road. The first floodlit game is a First Division match against Bolton.
First Division, Old Trafford. Whelan, Taylor 2, Edwards. The title clinched. This was the last championship the full Babes side would play for.
103 goals in 42 First Division games.
First Division champions: 64 points from 42 games (W28 D8 L6, 103 goals). Manager: Matt Busby.
1–2 against Aston Villa at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Matt Busby.
4–0 against Aston Villa at Old Trafford. Manager: Matt Busby. Scorers: T. Taylor 3, Berry.
The flight home from a European Cup quarter-final in Belgrade crashes on take-off at Munich-Riem. 23 die, among them eight players: Bent, Byrne, Colman, Edwards, Jones, Pegg, Taylor and Whelan.
1958–1958. 22 matches, 5 won, 7 drawn, 10 lost (23% wins).
0–2 against Bolton Wanderers at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Jimmy Murphy.

events.ti: A roof on the Stretford End
events.tx: The last of the four sides to be covered after the war.
3–1 against Leicester City at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Matt Busby. Scorers: Herd 2, Law. Law's turn and shot for the first is the goal the day is remembered for; Pat Crerand ran the midfield.
0–4 against Everton at Goodison Park. Manager: Matt Busby.
On the board since just after Munich, Edwards, a friend of Busby, builds a 54% holding for about £40000.
First Division, Elland Road. Connelly. The head-to-head that settled the race.
First Division, Old Trafford. Law 2, Best. The title was secured here while Leeds drew at Birmingham. United lost the last game at Villa Park 2–1 and still finished top on goal average.
First Division champions: 61 points from 42 games (W26 D9 L7, 89 goals). Manager: Matt Busby.
2–2 against Liverpool at Old Trafford. Shared after a draw. Manager: Matt Busby. Scorers: Best, Herd.
Rebuilt with a cantilever roof and the first private boxes at a British football ground, ready for the 1966 World Cup.
Old Trafford hosts three group matches of the 1966 World Cup.
First Division, Upton Park. Law 2, Best, Crerand, Foulkes, Charlton. Title clinched with a game to spare; United were 4–0 up in 25 minutes.
First Division champions: 60 points from 42 games (W24 D12 L6, 84 goals). Manager: Matt Busby.
3–3 against Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford. Shared after a draw. Manager: Matt Busby. Scorers: Charlton 2, Law.

European Cup semi-final, second leg, Bernabéu. Sadler 73, Foulkes 78; Pirri 32, Gento 41, Amancio 45 (Zoco og 42). 3–1 down on the night at half-time, 3–2 behind on aggregate; Busby told them they were only one goal away.

4–1 aet against Benfica at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Matt Busby. Scorers: Charlton 2, Best, Kidd. Stepney's save from Eusébio in the last minute of normal time kept it level. Kidd scored on his 19th birthday. First English winners.
1–2 on aggregate against Estudiantes de La Plata. Manager: Matt Busby.
1969–1970. 87 matches, 31 won, 33 drawn, 23 lost (36% wins).
1970–1971. 21 matches, 11 won, 3 drawn, 7 lost (52% wins).
The Red Devils nickname, borrowed from Salford rugby club, was on programmes and scarves in the 1960s. It enters the crest in 1970 and the crest reaches the shirt in 1971.
1971–1972. 81 matches, 30 won, 24 drawn, 27 lost (37% wins).
1972–1977. 228 matches, 107 won, 56 drawn, 65 lost (47% wins). 1 FA Cup, 1 Second Division title.
21st of 22 in the First Division.
Second Division champions: 61 points from 42 games (W26 D9 L7, 66 goals). Promoted. Manager: Tommy Docherty.

events.ti: The devil becomes a heraldic badge
events.tx: The College of Arms grants the red devil with trident as a badge to the Football League for United's use.
0–1 against Southampton at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Tommy Docherty.
2–1 against Liverpool at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Tommy Docherty. Scorers: Pearson, J. Greenhoff. Liverpool won the European Cup four days later in Rome.
1977–1981. 201 matches, 81 won, 64 drawn, 56 lost (40% wins). 1 Charity Shield (shared).
0–0 against Liverpool at Wembley. Shared after a draw. Manager: Dave Sexton.
2–3 against Arsenal at Wembley. Manager: Dave Sexton.
He succeeds his father, Louis, on his death. In 1984 he turns down Robert Maxwell's bid.
1981–1986. 292 matches, 146 won, 79 drawn, 67 lost (50% wins). 2 FA Cups, 1 Charity Shield.
1–2 aet against Liverpool at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Ron Atkinson.
FA Cup final, Wembley. Stapleton 55, Wilkins 72; Smith 14, Stevens 87. 'And Smith must score…' — he didn't; Bailey saved with his legs.

4–0 in the replay after 2–2 against Brighton & Hove Albion at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Ron Atkinson. Scorers: Robson 2, Whiteside, Mühren. Robson declined the penalty that would have given him a hat-trick and handed it to Muhren.
2–0 against Liverpool at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Ron Atkinson. Scorers: Robson 2.

1–0 aet against Everton at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Ron Atkinson. Scorers: Whiteside. Moran was initially refused a medal; the FA relented. Moran became the first man sent off in an FA Cup final; ten men held the champions, and Whiteside curled the winner past Southall in extra time.
0–2 against Everton at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Ron Atkinson.

1986–2013. 1496 matches, 893 won, 337 drawn, 266 lost (60% wins). 13 Premier League titles, 5 FA Cups, 4 League Cups, 10 Community Shields (inc. 1 shared), 2 UEFA Champions Leagues, 1 European Cup Winners' Cup, 1 European Super Cup, 1 Intercontinental Cup, 1 FIFA Club World Cup.
Edwards agrees to sell the club to Michael Knighton for £20 million; the sale falls through and Knighton joins the board instead.
FA Cup third round, City Ground. Robins 56. The goal usually credited with saving Ferguson's job.
FA Cup final, Wembley. Robson 35, Hughes 62, 113; O'Reilly 18, Wright 72, 92. Ian Wright came off the bench with a broken leg barely healed and scored twice.
1–0 in the replay after 3–3 against Crystal Palace at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Martin. Ferguson's first trophy at United, three and a half years after arriving.
1–1 against Liverpool at Wembley Stadium. Shared after a draw. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Blackmore.
0–1 against Sheffield Wednesday at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Alex Ferguson.

2–1 against Barcelona at Stadion Feijenoord. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Hughes 2. Hughes's second came from a narrow angle after rounding Busquets. Clayton Blackmore cleared off the line late on.
The listing on the London Stock Exchange raises £6.7 million.
1–0 against Red Star Belgrade at Old Trafford. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: McClair. Single leg because of the war in Yugoslavia.

1–0 against Nottingham Forest at Wembley Stadium. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: McClair. Giggs set it up. Forest had beaten United in the 1990 FA Cup quarter and the 1991 League Cup; this was the first final between the clubs.
The breakaway league starts with a 2–1 defeat at Sheffield United; United win the first title.

Premier League, Old Trafford. Bruce 86, 90+6; Hirst 65 (pen). Referee Michael Peck pulled a muscle and linesman John Hilditch took over, which is why seven minutes were added. 'Fergie time' was born here. A penalty down with the title slipping, then Bruce's header in the 86th and another seven minutes into stoppage time — Ferguson and Kidd on the pitch, and the first title in 26 years within reach.
Premier League, Old Trafford. Giggs 22, Ince 61, Pallister 90; Gallacher 8. The night the trophy was presented; Pallister's free-kick was his first goal of the season.
Premier League champions: 84 points from 42 games (W24 D12 L6, 67 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson.
1–1, 5–4 on penalties against Arsenal. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Hughes.
Terraces converted to seats; capacity falls to about 44000.
1–3 against Aston Villa. Manager: Alex Ferguson.

FA Cup semi-final replay, Maine Road. Irwin, Kanchelskis, Robson, Giggs; Pointon. Three days after Hughes's volley in the 119th minute had saved the first match at Wembley. Pointon put Oldham ahead in extra time; Hughes' volley with a minute of it left kept the Double alive. United won the replay 4–1.
Premier League, Old Trafford. Cantona 37, Giggs 59; Mathie 28. The next day Blackburn lost at Coventry and the title was retained.
92 points from 42 games in the Premier League.
Premier League champions: 92 points from 42 games (W27 D11 L4, 80 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson.
4–0 against Chelsea at Wembley (original). Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Cantona 2, Hughes, McClair. Goalless and under pressure at half-time; three goals in nine minutes after the break.
2–0 against Blackburn Rovers. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Cantona, Ince.
United 9–0 Ipswich Town (home), Premier League.
0–1 against Everton at Wembley (original). Manager: Alex Ferguson.
The 30-year-old North Stand is pulled down and a three-tier stand built in time for Euro 96, when Old Trafford hosts group games, a quarter-final and a semi-final.
Premier League, Old Trafford. Behind to Armstrong; Cole, Beckham and Cantona twice on New Year's Day.
Premier League, St James' Park. Cantona 51. Schmeichel's first half kept Newcastle out; the gap went to one point.
Premier League champions: 82 points from 38 games (W25 D7 L6, 73 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson. Final day. Keegan's 'I'd love it' interview had been a week earlier.

1–0 against Liverpool at Wembley (original). Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Cantona. James punched a corner out; Cantona, adjusting his body on the edge of the box, volleyed through the crowd. Liverpool's white suits are the other memory.
4–0 against Newcastle United. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Cantona, Butt, Beckham, Keane.

Premier League, St James' Park. Peacock, Ginola, Ferdinand, Shearer, Albert. The low point — followed by 6–3 at Southampton and a first home European defeat to Fenerbahçe. United still finished seven clear.

Premier League, Old Trafford. Keane 36, G. Neville 42, Solskjær 68; Juninho 15, Emerson 50, Hignett 61 (pen). The point that left Liverpool needing to win at Wimbledon the next night. They lost, Newcastle drew, and the title was United's.
Premier League champions: 75 points from 38 games (W21 D12 L5, 76 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson.
1–1, 4–2 on penalties against Chelsea. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Johnsen.
0–3 against Arsenal. Manager: Alex Ferguson.
The board accepts a £623 million offer from Rupert Murdoch's BSkyB. Shareholders United Against Murdoch, now the Manchester United Supporters' Trust, is formed to fight it.
FA Cup 4th round, Old Trafford. Owen after three minutes, then nothing until the 88th: Yorke from Beckham's free-kick, and Solskjær in stoppage time. The Treble's first escape.

FA Cup semi-final replay, Villa Park. Beckham 17, Giggs 109; Bergkamp 69. Keane sent off, Schmeichel saved Bergkamp's penalty in the last minute, then Giggs took the ball from Vieira in his own half and beat five players. Beckham's opener, Bergkamp's equaliser, Keane sent off, Schmeichel saves Bergkamp's last-minute penalty, then Giggs runs through half the Arsenal defence in extra time.

Champions League semi-final, second leg, Stadio delle Alpi. Keane 24, Yorke 34, Cole 83; Inzaghi 6, 11. Two down after eleven minutes. Keane's header, then his booking for a foul on Zidane. Inzaghi twice inside 11 minutes. Keane's header, Yorke's diving header and Cole's late winner, with Keane booked and out of the final — the night Ferguson called the most courageous performance he had seen.
The Monopolies and Mergers Commission stops the deal at the final hurdle.
Premier League champions: 79 points from 38 games (W22 D13 L3, 80 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson. Arsenal beat Villa 1–0 at the same time; one point separated them at the end.
2–0 against Newcastle United at Wembley (original). Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Sheringham, Scholes. Keane went off injured after eight minutes; Sheringham replaced him and scored within three.

2–1 against Bayern Munich. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Sheringham, Solskjær. Keane and Scholes suspended. Bayern hit the woodwork twice through Scholl and Jancker before the two corners. 'Football, bloody hell.' Basler's free-kick after six minutes, nothing for 84 more, then Sheringham from Giggs' scuff in the 91st and Solskjær's toe-poke from Sheringham's flick in the 93rd. The Treble.
1–2 against Arsenal. Manager: Alex Ferguson.
0–1 against Lazio. Manager: Alex Ferguson.
45 matches unbeaten in all competitions, 1998-12-26 to 1999-09-29 (W31 D14 L0).
1–0 against Palmeiras. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Keane. Giggs's run and cross; Keane at the far post. First British winners.
40 home matches unbeaten, 1998-12-26 to 2000-04-15 (W32 D8 L0).
Premier League, The Dell. Beckham 7, Solskjær 54, 78; Pahars 83. Title clinched with four games left.
Premier League champions: 91 points from 38 games (W28 D7 L3, 97 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson.
0–2 against Chelsea. Manager: Alex Ferguson.
The first team moves into the £14 million main building at Carrington in pre-season; the academy building follows in 2002.
Premier League, Old Trafford. Yorke 3, 18, 22, Keane 37, Solskjær 39, Sheringham 90; Henry 15. Arsenal's heaviest defeat under Wenger at that point.
Premier League, Old Trafford. Yorke 2, Giggs, Silvestre; Carsley, Hartson. The title was confirmed an hour before kick-off when Arsenal lost 3–0 at the Riverside.
Premier League champions: 80 points from 38 games (W24 D8 L6, 79 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson.
1–2 against Liverpool. Manager: Alex Ferguson.
Premier League, White Hart Lane. Three down at half-time at White Hart Lane; five goals in the second half, Verón's drive the fourth and Beckham's the fifth.
0–2 against Liverpool. Manager: Alex Ferguson.

Champions League quarter-final, second leg, Old Trafford. Van Nistelrooy 43, Helguera 52 (og), Beckham 71, 85; Ronaldo 12, 50, 59. Out of Europe, but the night Ronaldo was applauded off by Old Trafford and Beckham scored twice from the bench. Included because the season is unexplained without it. Ronaldo's hat-trick and a standing ovation from the Stretford End; Beckham off the bench with two. Won the night, lost the tie 5–6.
Premier League, Old Trafford. Van Nistelrooy 10, 50, 60, Beckham 33; Jensen 24. The next day Arsenal lost 3–2 at home to Leeds, and the title was United's.
Premier League champions: 83 points from 38 games (W25 D8 L5, 74 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson.
1–1, 4–3 on penalties against Arsenal. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Silvestre.
FA Cup semi-final, Villa Park. Scholes 32. The only domestic defeat of Arsenal's Invincibles season.
3–0 against Millwall at Millennium Stadium. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Ronaldo, Van Nistelrooy 2. Millwall were a First Division side managed by Dennis Wise.
1–3 against Arsenal. Manager: Alex Ferguson.

Buying the 28.7% held by John Magnier and J. P. McManus takes Malcolm Glazer's family to 57%; by 16 May they hold 75.7% and the club is delisted in June. Over £500 million of the price becomes the club's debt.
0–0 aet, 4–5 on penalties against Arsenal at Millennium Stadium. Manager: Alex Ferguson.
4–0 against Wigan Athletic. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Rooney 2, Saha, Ronaldo. Three goals in six second-half minutes.
New second tiers in the north-east and north-west quadrants take Old Trafford almost back to its original capacity.
Premier League, Goodison Park. Two down at Goodison with Chelsea closing in; O'Shea, a Neville own goal going the right way, Rooney and Eagles.
Champions League quarter-final, second leg, Old Trafford. Carrick 11, 60, Smith 17, Rooney 19, Ronaldo 44, 49, Evra 81; De Rossi 69. 4–0 up after 19 minutes.
Premier League, City of Manchester Stadium. Ronaldo 34 (pen). Chelsea's draw the next afternoon confirmed it.
Premier League champions: 89 points from 38 games (W28 D5 L5, 83 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson.
0–1 aet against Chelsea at Wembley (new). Manager: Alex Ferguson.
1–1, 3–0 on penalties against Chelsea. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Giggs.
On the 50th anniversary of the disaster the Old Trafford tunnel is renamed the Munich Tunnel.
Champions League semi-final, second leg, Old Trafford. Scholes 14. A Scholes strike from 25 yards, three years after he had missed the 2005 semi through suspension.
Premier League champions: 87 points from 38 games (W27 D6 L5, 80 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson. Final day; Giggs scored on his 758th appearance, equalling Charlton's record.

1–1, 6–5 on penalties against Chelsea. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Ronaldo. Drogba sent off in extra time for a slap on Vidić. Giggs, on for Scholes, broke Charlton's appearance record and scored the decisive penalty. Ronaldo's header, Lampard's equaliser, Drogba sent off in extra time; Ronaldo missed his penalty, Terry slipped, van der Sar saved from Anelka. Won 6–5 on penalties.
0–0, 3–1 on penalties against Portsmouth. Manager: Alex Ferguson.
1–2 against Zenit Saint Petersburg. Manager: Alex Ferguson.
1–0 against LDU Quito. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Rooney. Vidić sent off after 49 minutes; Rooney's winner from Ronaldo's pass with ten men.
0–0, 4–1 on penalties against Tottenham Hotspur. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Ben Foster saved Jamie O'Hara's kick after studying it on an iPod on the touchline; Giggs, Tevez, Ronaldo and Anderson scored.
Premier League, Old Trafford. Behind to Agbonlahor with half an hour left; Ronaldo's free-kick levelled it and Macheda, 17, on debut, turned and curled the winner in the 93rd.
Premier League, Old Trafford. Two down at half-time; a contested penalty started it and five went in inside 25 minutes.
Premier League, Old Trafford. —. The point that clinched the 18th title, three days after a 2–0 win at Wigan from 1–0 down.
Premier League champions: 90 points from 38 games (W28 D6 L4, 68 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson.
0–2 against Barcelona. Manager: Alex Ferguson.
2–2, 1–4 on penalties against Chelsea. Manager: Alex Ferguson.
Premier League, Old Trafford. City equalised three times, the last through Bellamy in the 90th; Owen's winner came in the 96th, with Hughes pointing at the board.
League Cup Semi-final, 2nd leg, Old Trafford. Level on aggregate with the tie heading to extra time; Rooney's header from Giggs' cross in the 92nd.
2–1 against Aston Villa. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Owen, Rooney. Owen pulled a hamstring just before half-time; Rooney replaced him and headed the winner from Valencia's cross.
3–1 against Chelsea. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Valencia, Hernández, Berbatov.
Premier League, Old Trafford. Nani 41, Rooney 78; Silva 65. The overhead kick from Nani's deflected cross.
Premier League, Ewood Park. Rooney 73 (pen); Emerton 20. The point that made it 19.
Premier League champions: 80 points from 38 games (W23 D11 L4, 78 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson.
1–3 against Barcelona. Manager: Alex Ferguson.
3–2 against Manchester City. Manager: Alex Ferguson. Scorers: Smalling, Nani 2.
The North Stand is renamed for Ferguson's 25 years as manager.
The Glazers sell part of their holding in an IPO on the New York Stock Exchange, keeping control.
Premier League, Old Trafford. Van Persie 2, 13, 33. The 20th title. The second goal — Rooney's 40-yard pass, Van Persie's first-time volley — was the Premier League's Goal of the Season.
Premier League, Old Trafford. Chicharito 39, Ferdinand 87; Michu 49. Ferguson's last home match; the trophy presented afterwards. Ferdinand's winner was his first league goal in five years.
Premier League champions: 89 points from 38 games (W28 D5 L5, 86 goals). Manager: Alex Ferguson.
2013–2014. 51 matches, 27 won, 9 drawn, 15 lost (53% wins). 1 Community Shield.
2–0 against Wigan Athletic. Manager: David Moyes. Scorers: Van Persie 2.
2014–2014. 4 matches, 2 won, 1 drawn, 1 lost (50% wins).
His sons, led by co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer, keep the club.
2014–2016. 103 matches, 54 won, 25 drawn, 24 lost (52% wins). 1 FA Cup.
The South Stand is renamed before the home game against Everton, 60 years after Charlton's debut.
FA Cup semi-final, Wembley. Fellaini 34, Martial 90+3; Smalling 75 (og). De Gea saved Lukaku's penalty; Martial finished a counter in added time.
2–1 aet against Crystal Palace at Wembley (new). Manager: Louis van Gaal. Scorers: Mata, Lingard. Lingard's volley from the edge of the box, with United down to ten.
2016–2018. 144 matches, 84 won, 32 drawn, 28 lost (58% wins). 1 UEFA Europa League, 1 League Cup, 1 Community Shield.
2–1 against Leicester City. Manager: José Mourinho. Scorers: Lingard, Ibrahimović.

3–2 against Southampton. Manager: José Mourinho. Scorers: Ibrahimović 2, Lingard. Southampton had a Gabbiadini goal wrongly disallowed at 0–0 and came back from 2–0 down; Ibrahimović's late header from Herrera's cross.
2–0 against Ajax. Manager: José Mourinho. Scorers: Pogba, Mkhitaryan. Pogba's deflected shot, then Mkhitaryan's hooked finish from a corner. United had 31% of the ball and won comfortably.
1–2 against Real Madrid. Manager: José Mourinho.
0–1 against Chelsea at Wembley Stadium. Manager: José Mourinho.
The club's professional women's team is formed and starts in the Championship.
2018–2021. 168 matches, 91 won, 37 drawn, 40 lost (54% wins).
United 9–0 Southampton (home), Premier League.
United join 11 other clubs as founder members; they withdraw two days later after a backlash from fans and government.
Fans protesting against the Glazers get into Old Trafford; it is the first Premier League match postponed because of supporter protests.
1–1, 10–11 on penalties against Villarreal. Manager: Ole Gunnar Solskjær.
2021–2021. 3 matches, 2 won, 1 drawn, 0 lost (67% wins).
2021–2022. 29 matches, 11 won, 10 drawn, 8 lost (38% wins).
2022–2024. 128 matches, 70 won, 23 drawn, 35 lost (55% wins). 1 FA Cup, 1 League Cup.

events.ti: Glazers open the club to bids
events.tx: Sir Jim Ratcliffe of INEOS and Sheikh Jassim are the two declared bidders for control.
Premier League, Old Trafford. Fernandes 78, Rashford 82; Grealish 60. The derby that marked the season's high point — and the Rashford offside argument.
2–0 against Newcastle. Manager: Erik ten Hag. Scorers: Casemiro, Rashford. Casemiro's header from Shaw's free-kick; Rashford's shot deflected in off Botman six minutes later.
United 0–7 Liverpool (away), Premier League. The joint heaviest in the club's history.
